Description: TRANSFERRED FROM MARCO: Food Price Transmission Analysis — Import Substitution Buffer Identified. Despite -155K ag workers (MARCO VX-2.02 BREACHED) and 75% workforce no-shows in CA fields, fresh produce inflation is only +0.3% YoY (Dec 2025) — LOWEST food category vs +3.1% overall food. July 2025 wholesale vegetable spike of +38.9% (biggest summer spike in century — lettuce +133%, spinach +157%, broccoli +41%) did NOT transmit to consumer prices.
Analysis: KEY FINDING: Three buffers absorbing latent food price pressure: (1) MEXICAN IMPORT SUBSTITUTION — Mexico supplies 63% of US vegetable imports, 70% of fresh tomatoes; farm labor costs 10-20% of US; (2) RETAILER ABSORPTION — grocers eating costs to stay competitive; (3) VOLATILITY SMOOTHING — wholesale produce naturally volatile, retailers don't pass through short spikes. MSU Study: 10% employment decline should = ~3% food price increase, but seeing ~0.3%. IMPLICATION FOR CARL: Food costs NOT currently stressing consumers, but latent pressure exists. Transmission triggers: tariff increases (currently 17-25% on Mexican produce), import capacity maxed, retailer margin exhaustion, Mexican supply disruption. This is a COMPRESSED SPRING — stable until buffer fails, then rapid transmission.
Data Quote: Fresh produce +0.3% YoY (Dec 2025) vs +3.1% overall food; July 2025 wholesale +38.9% (corrected -15.1% in Aug); Mexico 63% vegetable imports, 70% tomatoes; MSU model: 10% employment decline = 3% price increase
Source: MSU Study (Rutledge); BLS CPI/PPI; USDA ERS; ABC News; Blue Book Services; Xinhua; MARCO Session 6 research
Cross Links: MARCO VX-MARCO-2.07 (retired); MARCO ML-WFD-09, ML-WFD-11; VX-CARL-3.04 (Savings Buffer); VX-CARL-4.03 (Trade-Down)
CARL Relevance: INDIRECT (CURRENTLY): Food NOT stressing consumers now. But: (1) Latent pressure exists — July wholesale spike proves stress is real but buffered. (2) Buffer failure would rapidly increase food costs. (3) Trade-down behavior (VX-CARL-4.03) may reflect food cost pressure not captured in CPI. (4) Food inflation would compound savings buffer exhaustion (VX-CARL-3.04).
Transmission Type: LATENT (buffered stress, not transmitting); Could become DIRECT if tariffs increase or buffers fail
Notes: DOMAIN TRANSFER: Food price tracking transferred from MARCO to CARL effective 2026-01-22. MARCO retains ag WORKFORCE tracking (labor shortage, wages) as population movement issue. CARL owns CONSUMER FOOD COST tracking as cost-of-living burden. Recommend CARL create VX-CARL-2.07 (Food Cost Burden) to track this formally. Current status: NORMAL (buffered). Watch triggers: tariff escalation, Mexican supply disruption, retailer margin capitulation.
